result.keywords: We study the problem of computing efficient approximate repairs for inconsistent relational data under functional dependencies and related integrity constraints, combining techniques from database repair and incremental processing. We consider both subset-style repairs based on tuple deletions and update-style repairs based on cell modifications, with an emphasis on algorithmic tradeoffs between exactness and approximation. Our results identify tractable families of constraints where a repair can be found in polynomial time, and hard families where approximation guarantees are limited. We also analyze weighted tuples, duplicate tuples, and incremental maintenance under changing constraints, and we relate our findings to prior work on dichotomies for database consistency and probabilistic satisfaction models.
result.title: Approximate Repair Planning for Constraint-Heavy Dataflows.
